extracted.subtask_description: A chapter of a contemporary techno-thriller / YA novel combining urban protest/gameplay scenes, surveillance-evading tradecraft, and commentary on urban design. The page includes in-world game rules, tactical guidance for evasion, and narrative exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: VampMob: stay-in-game biting frequency and elimination
rubrics_metrics.description: You need to bite as many other vampires as you can in order to stay in the game. If one minute goes by without a bite, you're out. Once you're out, turn your shirt around backwards and go referee -- watch two or three vamps to see if they're getting their bites in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanic defines elimination condition (one minute without a bite) and post-elimination duty (become referee, wear shirt backwards).

rubrics_metrics.name: VampMob: how to 'bite' another vamp
rubrics_metrics.description: To bite another vamp, you have to say 'Bite!' five times before they do. So you run up to a vamp, make eye-contact, and shout 'bite bite bite bite bite!' and if you get it out before she does, you live and she crumbles to dust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the concrete action and success condition for scoring a 'bite' (verbal ritual + speed).

rubrics_metrics.name: VampMob: clan/team and non-consumptive blood rule
rubrics_metrics.description: You and the other vamps you meet at your rendezvous are a team. They are your clan. You derive no nourishment from their blood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes social structure (clans/teams) and clarifies it's a game (no actual harm).

rubrics_metrics.name: VampMob: invisibility mechanic
rubrics_metrics.description: You can 'go invisible' by standing still and folding your arms over your chest. You can't bite invisible vamps, and they can't bite you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines a safe/untargetable status and how to achieve it (standing still, arms folded).

rubrics_metrics.name: VampMob: honor-system play and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: This game is played on the honor system. The point is to have fun and get your vamp on, not to win.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes voluntary compliance and social norms over formal enforcement; sets tone and intent of play.

rubrics_metrics.name: VampMob: endgame whisper-campaign propagation
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an end-game that will be passed by word of mouth as winners begin to emerge. The game-masters will start a whisper campaign among the players when the time comes. Spread the whisper as quickly as you can and watch for the sign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies that final-stage instructions are disseminated orally and must be rapidly propagated among players (viral whisper mechanism).

rubrics_metrics.name: Urban design: mixed-use, diversity, and 'eyes on the street'
rubrics_metrics.description: Real cities are organic and they have a lot of variety -- rich and poor, white and brown, Anglo and Mex, retail and residential and even industrial. A neighborhood like that has all kinds of people passing through it at all hours of the day or night, so you get businesses that cater to every need, you get people around all the time, acting like eyes on the street.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Positive criteria for healthy urban neighborhoods (diversity of uses and people, continuous activity, natural surveillance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Urban design anti-pattern: single-use zoning creates dead spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Neighborhoods consisting of one kind of building (e.g., civic centers with court houses, museums, and civic buildings) become empty by night and resemble malls rather than living neighborhoods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how top-down planning and single-function districts lead to lack of 24-hour activity, social isolation, and decline (a 'ghost-town' effect).

rubrics_metrics.name: Endgame dispersal tactic: feign being gassed
rubrics_metrics.description: Endgame: when the cops order us to disperse, pretend you've been gassed. Pass it on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactical instruction for crowd dispersal moments: simulate incapacitation (e.g., clutch throat, retch) to blend with others and avoid detection or arrest; distribute the tactic by telling others verbally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disguise and rapid wardrobe-change tradecraft
rubrics_metrics.description: Wardrobe change: strip off jacket and turn it inside out, produce a wool hat and pull it over hair, use make-up remover wipes and clean nails, change into different clothes quickly (lose the shoes, jacket, hat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical steps for rapid on-street disguise to alter appearance and reduce chance of recognition by witnesses or cameras; emphasizes speed (total time less than a minute).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Faraday pouch for IDs and cards
rubrics_metrics.description: Put your student card, ATM card, Fast Pass into a silvered bag, a radio-proof Faraday pouch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational security measure to isolate electronic IDs/trackers and prevent remote scanning/tracking of transit/credit/ID cards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gait-recognition countermeasure: pebbles in shoes
rubrics_metrics.description: "Put these pebbles in your shoes before you put them on -- 'It's OK. I sprained my foot. No gait recognition program will spot me now.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical deception to alter gait signature to defeat automated gait-recognition systems (introduce limp or altered step).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phone handling to preserve evidence and avoid tracking
rubrics_metrics.description: Cancel the photo-deletion on a phone, turn off its radio, set the sleep timer to the longest setting (two hours) to avoid needing a password to wake, and keep tapping the keypad periodically; switch off your phone when advised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps combine evidence preservation (cancel deletion), battery/lock management, and operational security (turning off radios to avoid location tracking). Notes limitations (can't disable password without knowing it) and trade-offs (must tap periodically).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use payphones and sanitize physical traces (coins) for anonymous communication
rubrics_metrics.description: Call from a payphone, put hood up so CCTV won't get a photo; polish a quarter to remove fingerprints before use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low-tech anonymity and trace-reduction tactics for contacting reporters or others without leaving biometric/CCTV evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority-appearance tactic to bypass checkpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenting a convincing badge/credential (Masha held up a badge) causes officers to 'melt away' and leave passage open.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social-engineering tactic: assume or display authoritative appearance/credentials to persuade enforcement to stand down—high-risk but effective if credential looks legitimate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious handing over IDs to untrusted actors
rubrics_metrics.description: As she put them in her pocket, I realized I'd just turned my ID over to her. If she was on the other side...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational caution: surrendering ID or sensitive materials to others can be exploited; retain control of identifying documents unless the recipient is fully trusted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and use documentary evidence when engaging media
rubrics_metrics.description: I had to call Barbara Stratford, tell her what had happened. Show her the photo of Darryl. The VampMob had to have freaked people out; Barbara found some photos and ran them alongside an investigative piece about 'Gitmo-by-the-Bay'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalistic strategy: collect photos/videos that corroborate claims and present them to an investigative reporter to generate public exposure; documented proof increases credibility and impact.
